To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the spin dynamics of the A15 Cs3C60 phase is characterized by a Korringa-like constant, that is, by a metallic behavior of the spin dynamics, and that this Korringa constant is markedly enhanced below pc, the pressure for which the A15 phase becomes a superconductor, as well as above pc, where the A15 phase is a superconductor but the spin dynamics is not metallic.

1) the Korringa constant in the A15 phase is in agreement with the Korringa law expected from the metallic state, but 2) the Korringas constant in the fcc phase is larger than expected, and 3) the T1T behavior in the A15 Cs3C60 phase is similar to that observed in the A3C60 phases, which is consistent with the fact that Cs3C60 is a metallic Mott insulator, and
the spin-lattice relaxation rate of the 133Cs nuclei in Cs3C60 is strongly enhanced at the superconducting transition temperature Tc and in the superconducting state.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the electronic properties of the fullerene-based superconducting compounds Cs3C60 and Rb3C60.
the physics of the Mott insulator/superconductor transition in the A3C60 phases.
the electronic properties of a new class of materials, the fullerides, in which the intermolecular interactions play a crucial role.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the superconducting state of the Cs 3C60 compounds is not of the BCS type, but rather of the BEC type, with the superfluid density arising from the condensation of the spinon Fermi sea.
, at ppc, the Cs3C6O superconducting phases are characterized by the presence of a Mott insulating ground state, which is destroyed by the application of a hydrostatic pressure.
the Mott physics in the fcc-Cs3 C60 superconducting phase is not drastically different from the one in the A15 phase, but that the latter is more sensitive to pressure variations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Cs3C fullerenes are a unique playground where one can evidence in the same material the effects of electronic correlations on the spin dynamics at the MOTT transition and in the superconducting phase.
the Cs3C fullerenes are a unique system to study the interplay of Mott physics and superconductivity.
the Mott transition in Cs3C60 is a critical phenomenon, and it is not surprising to find that it is reflected in the spin dynamics of the metallic phase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a Mott transition can occur in a superconducting state, and it is not necessary for a metal to become insulating before it becomes a superconductor.

the NMR data in the A3C60 superconductor phases can be understood in terms of a simple model in which the superconducting gap is small and the Mott transition is driven by the interplay of the Coulomb interaction and the lattice.

the Cs3C6 superconductor is a strongly correlated system with a Mott transition at pc, where the superconducting pairing mechanism has to be sought in the vicinity of this Mott transition, and not in a conventional BCS scenario.
